items.title: Pete Levin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: And I’ve worked with several people over the years that I really think of as pure artists. Gil Evans is one, Gerry Mulligan

ctx.x: Well it made a big impression on him but not on you I guess.

Well it’s a job. And I enjoyed it while I was doing it. It distracts from things that you might like to do. And I’ve worked with several people over the years that I really think of as pure artists. Gil Evans is one, Gerry Mulligan, people who just — I’m going to do this, this is what I do. Gil was constantly turning down offers for professorships. He just said no, I don’t want to do that, I’ve got a gig Monday night playing at Sweet Basil’s. I can’t be up in Massachusetts. So that’s it. Nice to strive for that.…

Well I wish you the best of luck in maybe arriving in Woodstock, and with wherever those future projects take you. It’s been fascinating talking to you. I think we could probably do another one down the road and see where you go. All right?
